title: Squad battle units render as KayKit models with KayKit animations
description:
Squad battle units are still primitive capsules (combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd:_build_visual, :282). Swap them for KayKit models driven by KayKit animations. Assets are staged by the director under combat/battle/models/kaykit/ (CC0; CREDITS.md row exists). Do not add or download other assets.

## Mapping (director decisions, do not redesign)
Allies (faction ally):
- knight -> characters/Knight.glb, weapon sword_1handed + shield (round or badge) in hand slots
- mage -> characters/Mage.glb, weapon staff
- ranger -> characters/Ranger.glb, weapon bow_withString
- rogue -> characters/Rogue.glb, dagger in each hand
- cleric -> characters/Mage.glb + wand (PROVISIONAL, no free cleric model; game-designer call later)
Enemies (faction enemy): knight -> Skeleton_Warrior (+Skeleton_Blade, Skeleton_Shield_Small_A), rogue -> Skeleton_Rogue (+Skeleton_Blade), mage -> Skeleton_Mage (+Skeleton_Staff), ranger -> Skeleton_Rogue (+Skeleton_Crossbow).
Use the model's own hand bone attachments (BoneAttachment3D on handslot.r / handslot.l or whatever the rig names them; read the rig, do not guess).

Clips (all Rig_Medium, one shared AnimationLibrary loaded once, static, not re-imported per unit):
- idle: Idle_A (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Idle)
- moving: Running_A (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Walking)
- attack/lunge: knight Melee_1H_Attack_Chop, rogue Melee_Dualwield_Attack_Stab, ranger Ranged_Bow_Release (skeleton ranger: Ranged_1H_Shoot), mage and cleric Ranged_Magic_Shoot
- hit (_react / recoil): Hit_A, critical Hit_B
- dead: Death_A then hold last frame (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Death then hold)
- downed ally: Death_B then hold; revive back to idle
Clips must play in place. If a clip moves the root, pin it; report which ones did.

## Keep
HP bars, chip, selection/elite/telegraph rings, guard bubble, downed marker, lunge, recoil, hit-stop, set_time_scale (animation speed must follow _time_scale()). Public API of BattleUnitView unchanged: set_actor, hit_stop, set_time_scale, lunge, set_selected.
## Replace
Capsule body/head/legs and _add_archetype_silhouette primitives. Death pivot tilt (DEAD_TILT) and squash are replaced by the clips; delete constants that become unused (no warnings). Faction must stay readable (heroes vs skeletons is enough; keep rings).

## Acceptance
1. BUILT: tests/import_gate.ps1 exit 0, zero errors/warnings. GUT full suite green with the APPDATA prefix from CLAUDE.md. Update test_battle_unit_view.gd assertions that checked capsule/tilt internals to assert the new behavior (correct clip name playing per state), do not delete coverage.
2. Headless still works: models load under --headless without errors.
3. Perf: run .agent-results/ig-544/ui/benchmark_fallen_citadel.gd (50-unit) before and after; report both frame-time numbers. >2x slower = stop and report, do not optimize creatively.
4. A rendered screenshot of a live battle with all 4 ally archetypes and skeleton enemies, saved under .agent-results/<bead-id>/.
Non-goals: arena (combat/arena) and hub avatar stay on their current models. No new autoload. No gameplay/simulation changes (battle_simulation.gd untouched).
Engine: you get the engine alone; kill every Godot process you start and confirm Get-Process Godot* is empty before returning.
Boundary: scene<->script seam -> verifier pass mandatory after.

title: Battle view: smooth live playback, punchier effects, smaller damage numbers
description:
Owner play-test 2026-09-23: movement looks choppy, battle feels too fast, hit-stop / lunge / wave-clear slow-mo not noticeable, damage numbers a bit big. HP bars OK.

ROOT CAUSE (director): live battles advance in 0.25s chunks (GameSession EXPEDITION_PULSE_SECONDS, systems/game_session.gd:21) and the view polls every 0.25s (BATTLE_PULSE_SECONDS, combat/battle/battle_view.gd:20). So 2-3 sim ticks land at once. Units then exponential-lerp (battle_unit_view.gd:201, rate 8/s): dash then stop, 4x a second. Every hit in the chunk fires on the same frame, so 0.06s hit-stop and lunges overlap and vanish.

FIX (view only, sim untouched, no save keys):
1. Live mode plays back one pulse behind: positions move linearly from the last snapshot to the new one over the pulse, no dash-and-stop. Practice mode (every frame) must stay correct.
2. VFX events play at their own tick time inside the pulse (offset = (event tick - first tick) * battle_tick_seconds), not all on one frame.
3. Punch tuning so each is visible: hit-stop, lunge distance, wave-clear slow-mo length/scale. Pick values, list old->new.
4. Damage numbers ~25-30% smaller (normal and crit); crit stays clearly bigger than normal.
Do NOT change battle pace/sim speed: owner re-judges pace after smoothing.

ACCEPT: BUILT (import gate + full GUT with APPDATA redirect) green; tests for the interpolation and event offset; no Engine.time_scale; real save untouched; no Godot left running.
notes: 2026-09-24 applied (view-only). Unit: linear glide from drawn position to new sim position over one render interval (live BATTLE_PULSE_SECONDS 0.25, practice battle_tick_seconds 0.1), first placement snaps (fixes fly-in from origin); per-unit reaction_delay so flash/recoil/squash/death play at the unit's hit tick. View: events_between stamps tick; delay=(tick-first_tick)*step, step=min(tick_s, glide/ticks) so hitches squeeze inside the interval; queue in _process (real time); slow-mo waits for last death; basic_attack carries target crit. Tuning: HIT_STOP 0.06->0.1, LUNGE_DISTANCE 0.3->0.5, LUNGE_BACK 0.15->0.2, SLOW_MO_SCALE 0.35->0.25, SLOW_MO_SECONDS 0.4->0.8, damage font 56->40, crit 90->64, outline 10->8. BUILT: gate clean, GUT redirected 375/375 (+9). No Engine.time_scale.

title: Arena attack clips are stretched 3-4x to fit the balance windows; trim them instead
description:
Root cause of 'combat feels clunky' after the Mixamo swap (played 2026-09-05, play pass 4).

arena.gd:_play_animation() sets custom_speed = animation.length / target_duration, so every
attack plays the WHOLE Mixamo clip (stance -> windup -> swing -> return to stance) squeezed
into the balance window that was authored for capsules. Measured native lengths (headless,
2026-09-05) against the windows they are forced into:

  Attack_A  1.500 s -> 0.42 s  (3.6x)   light chain
  Attack_B  1.667 s -> 0.42 s  (4.0x)
  Attack_C  1.367 s -> 0.42 s  (3.3x)
  Attack_Heavy 1.000 s -> 0.92 s (1.1x) -- the one that reads fine, and the user agrees
  Standing Dodge Fwd/L/R ~1.0 s -> 0.38 s (2.6x); Backward 1.633 s -> 0.38 s (4.3x)
  Block (enemy parry) 1.400 s -> 0.20 s (7x, a twitch)
  Attack_A (enemy) 1.500 s -> 1.10 s (1.4x) -- but peak extension does not land at the
    0.55 s active onset SYSTEMS.md 'the t ~= 0.55 s alignment target' rules it should
  Hit_Chest (hero) plays at NATIVE 0.767 s but hit stun is 0.35 s, so Idle cuts it in half
  Block (hero) native 1.4 s, parry lasts ~0.65 s, cut mid-raise

The 0.06 s crossfade is a hard cut at 4x. The heavy is the proof: the one clip near native
speed is the one that feels right.

Fix, smallest that works: a per-clip trim table {clip: [start_s, end_s]} in arena.gd.
In _bind_animation_libraries set animation.length = end (Godot Animation has no trim API)
and in _play_animation seek(start) after play(). Stretch the TRIMMED swing segment into the
window, not the whole clip. The Mixamo attacks have ~0.5-0.7 s of actual swing, so light
attacks land near 1.3x instead of 4x. Give hero Hit_Chest a target_duration of
arena_enemy_hit_stun. Trim enemy Block to the shield raise (~0.3 s). Set the enemy Attack_A
trim so its peak lands at t = 0.55 s, which also closes the SYSTEMS.md alignment target.

The trim values need eyes on each clip in the editor (or a played guess, then tune). That
is the authored step; the code is ~20 lines. No AnimationTree, no new clips, no balance
changes. ig-e5u (AnimationTree, 8-way) stays separate and blocked on the backpedal asset.

Acceptance: import gate + GUT green; test_arena.gd's hit-stop resume test still passes
(seek after play must not break assigned_animation resume); a played light chain reads as
three swings, not three twitches; enemy contact reads as caused by the visible blade.
Boundary: none crossed (no save, no scene rename, no autoload). verifier optional.
notes:
2026-09-05 code landed, uncommitted, awaiting a played pass.
Director re-ran both gates on the final tree: import_gate.ps1 exit 0; GUT 204/204 passing.
Files: combat/arena/arena.gd (CLIP_TRIMS table, length trim in bind, seek-on-fresh-start in _play_animation, hero Hit_Chest fitted to arena_enemy_hit_stun), tests/unit/test_arena.gd (span helper, 1 new test).
Stretch now: lights ~1.1-1.7x (was 3.3-4x), dodges ~1.6x (was 2.6-4.3x), enemy Block 1x (was 7x), enemy Attack_A contact at 0.5395 s vs the 0.55 s target.

Finding: Block is a held guard pose with no raise motion at all. A real shield raise needs a new clip; out of scope.

Known ceiling: _play_animation decides 'fresh start' by assigned_animation changing. That is only correct because the state machine always plays Idle/locomotion for at least one frame between two uses of the same clip. If a future state ever chains the same clip back to back, the second play starts from the clip's frame 0 (stance) instead of the trim start. ponytail: fix then by also treating a finished clip as fresh.

Close when a played pass says the light chain reads as swings and enemy contact reads as caused by the blade. Trim values may then move.

title: Combat punch pack: hit-stop, lunge, squash, corpse fling, last-kill slow-mo, compact health bars
description: Owner picks 2026-09-23 (ideas 2,4,5,6,7) plus small health bars that don't clutter. View-only. The sim, snapshot and saves are untouched. Full spec in notes.
acceptance_criteria: See the dispatch brief in notes.
notes:
DISPATCH BRIEF (director, 2026-09-23). View-only. No creative work beyond this; ask instead.
FILES: combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_vfx.gd. Nothing else. NEVER touch battle_simulation.gd, battle_actor.gd, battle_state.gd, saves, .tscn, project.godot.
BUILDS ON ig-0gt (crit tick, red/yellow numbers, recoil on pivot x/z). Read its final code first.

OFFSETS RULE: recoil, lunge and fling all move the pivot on x/z. Keep a separate Vector3 offset per effect and set pivot.position = their sum (plus the death lift on y) in one place. No two tweens may write pivot.position directly.

2 HIT-STOP: on a hit event with critical=true, freeze the target's view animation (lerp + its tweens) for 0.06s. If a basic_attack event in the same render targets it, freeze that attacker too. Non-crit hits: no freeze.
4 LUNGE: on a basic_attack event where the attacker's archetype is not ranger/mage: lunge offset 0.3 toward the target over 0.07s, back to 0 over 0.15s (ease-out).
5 SQUASH: on a hit: pivot scale (1.15, 0.85, 1.15) back to ONE over 0.12s. On a crit: (1.25, 0.75, 1.25). Not on dead units once the death pose has started.
6 CORPSE FLING: on life alive->dead: fling offset slides along -facing during the 0.35s tip-over, 0.8 units if last_crit_tick advanced in that render, else 0.25, plus a small y arc peaking at 0.3. It must end at rest. A first-sight dead unit snaps (no fling).
7 LAST-KILL SLOW-MO: when a render takes the living enemy count from >0 to 0, the battle VIEW runs at 0.35x for 0.4s of real time. That covers unit lerps and every tween in units and vfx. NEVER use Engine.time_scale (it slows GameSession clocks for every expedition). NEVER scale the delta passed to BattleSimulation.advance in practice mode.
HEALTH BARS (replaces the current _hp_fill box):
- Billboarded, unshaded, drawn over geometry (no depth test) so bodies never hide it. Centered at y 2.2. 0.7 wide x 0.07 tall. Enemies with elite: 0.85 wide.
- Layers: a background 1a1a1a at alpha 0.6; a trailing damage chip f5e6a8 that eases down to the new value over 0.4s after a hit; a fill 6fcf6f for allies / e8483c for enemies.
- Visibility, to cut clutter: shown when hp < max_hp OR selected. Hidden at full hp. Hidden when dead. Hidden when downed (the downed marker covers that case).
- Heals: the fill rises immediately and the chip snaps to it.
TESTS: each effect's trigger and non-trigger case, the offsets-sum rule (a recoil during a lunge ends at zero), bar visibility rules, the chip trailing behavior (Tween.custom_step, no wall-clock waits), and slow-mo leaves the practice sim delta untouched.
DONE: import_gate clean + the APPDATA-redirected GUT command from CLAUDE.md, Get-Process Godot* empty, checkpoint with --append-notes (don't close), STATUS to "Main director [949b01]".
Assigned: Opus::high 2 game. Draft only until ig-0gt releases the engine AND its files.
2026-09-23 director rulings: Q1 slow-mo on every wave clear (literal); Q2 scale CPUParticles3D.speed_scale too; Q3 hit-stop counts real time. Go given; baseline 342/342.
2026-09-23 impl landed (uncommitted). Files: battle_unit_view.gd, battle_view.gd, battle_vfx.gd, test_battle_unit_view.gd, test_battle_vfx.gd only. title: Playtest timed expedition and recovery pacing
description:
## Objective
Determine whether the provisional timed expedition and active recovery pacing makes building multiple teams and recovering lost gear practical in a played session.

## Existing context
ig-6l4 implements concurrent reserved teams, finite and safe repeat orders, automatic rewards, and bulk management. docs/SYSTEMS.md defines base seconds 60/180/300, five-hero floors 15/45/75, square-root strength scaling, and the 5/team_size workload factor. Recovery uses 900 + 300*Reliquary active seconds and pauses on new losses. Automated formula examples are not playtest evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
Record a fresh three-pull save progressing to its second viable team; compare one geared squad with several squads; play a lost-gear recovery scenario with a surviving weak roster at low and high Reliquary levels. Record roster/gear, destinations, elapsed active time, income, idle periods, and decisions. Give an evidence-backed keep/change recommendation for the director. Do not change balance during the measurement. If later balance changes are authorized, run powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\import_gate.ps1 and the full unit suite on that final state.

## Files allowed to change
.agent-results/ig-6l4-pacing/ evidence only; this Bead's notes. Production balance/spec edits need a separately accepted decision.

title: Timed expeditions, team presets, and bulk management
description:
Objective: replace click-speed expedition farming with concurrent timed dispatches so roster depth and equipped strength improve sustained returns. The user explicitly requested timers, named team presets, send-X-times/auto-repeat, and bulk resource management. This is Astra's proposed direction pending user decisions and a decision-complete Plan-mode specification; it is not an accepted implementation plan.

Each hero may participate in one active expedition. Separate teams run concurrently without an energy meter or arbitrary small dispatch cap. Equipped heroes and their gear are reserved while away, with no mid-run transfers or sacrifice. Show duration before dispatch; derive it from current team strength against mission difficulty with diminishing gains and a nonzero floor. Exact timing and reward tuning are provisional and must cover a fresh save with only three pulls and compare solo with full-team efficiency because current enemies scale with team size.

Preserve combat and permadeath: a past clear is history, not proof of safety. Derive any Safe label from conservative worst-case attrition for the current roster, gear, and zone, including retreat threshold, and validate it before trusting it. Named presets require durable hero identities rather than names or indices, show missing or busy members, and never silently substitute. Preset launch offers one run, a finite total run count, and eventually until-stopped looping. Repeat orders recheck availability and safety, stop on casualty, retreat, or an incomplete team, and support stop-after-current-run. Credit rewards automatically. A dispatch board shows team, zone, remaining time, completed/ordered runs, and cumulative rewards, with collectable reports for review.

Clock behavior awaits the user's async answer. Astra's proposed default is that dispatched missions finish while closed while repeats run only while open; alternatives are session-only timing or bounded repeats progressing offline. Do not assume an answer.

Recovery remains unresolved. The current global expedition-turn clock would let parallel or automatic returns rapidly expire lost gear. Before implementation, explicitly redesign expiry and damage aging while preserving a meaningful Reliquary benefit; do not silently retain or replace the existing rule.

Bulk QoL reuses existing batch salvage/sacrifice and filters. Add protection for favorites, preset members, away heroes, and equipped gear; selection by rank, type, slot, and availability; clear destructive previews with outputs; quantity/all-eligible salvage and sacrifice; and batch part conversion with a keep-at-least reserve. The user's word refine is ambiguous among salvage, part conversion, and enhancement; identify the intended meaning before creating any resource system. No automatic destructive processing by default.

Scope implementation only after design acceptance: (1) timed persisted dispatch, reservations, presets, and finite repeats as one complete player loop; (2) richer bulk management and advanced automation. Existing ig-544 (controlled playable expeditions) and ig-yzc (hop into a sent run) are related direction, but neither grants scope for this work and neither is changed by this epic.

Technical entry points are hub/hub.gd:_on_expedition_pressed/_do_expedition, hub/expedition/expedition.gd:resolve, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, and heroes/hero.gd. Saves are version 1 with no durable hero IDs or migration machinery, and current resolution performs multiple automatic saves. Design exactly-once rewards and casualties, deterministic restart behavior, version-1 migration, and stable completion ordering for concurrent returns. Keep the three-autoload cap, central kill_hero path, and SaveService ownership. Change the explicit no-clock/no-offline-accrual spec only through an accepted plan. In Default mode, do not implement this complex epic until a decision-complete Plan-mode plan is accepted or the user explicitly overrides that gate.

Eventual acceptance: run tests/import_gate.ps1 and the full GUT suite; add focused reservation, repeat, timer, and migration tests plus actual isolated-APPDATA save/reload checks for in-flight missions, duplicate-return prevention, and old saves; visually check populated and empty dispatch boards. Do not mutate the user's save, run concurrent Godot processes, or perform git operations, commits, or pushes. This design/source-inspection turn establishes no runtime proof.

Do not close this epic until all core, UI, verification, save/reload, and review gates are complete.

1. Identity/schema: Save version 2. Hero and Item gain stable random serialized instance_id:String and favorite:bool=false. Legacy v1 missing IDs migrate once. Names and indices are never identity. Persist GameSession team_presets:Array[Dictionary], expedition_orders:Array[Dictionary], expedition_reports:Array[Dictionary], recovery_clock_seconds:float, recovery_clock_paused:bool. 2. Reservations/protection: one hero may be in at most one active order; unlimited disjoint orders. Shared backend guards prevent busy heroes from equip/unequip/rank-up/sacrifice/recovery/arena availability and prevent touching busy equipped gear. kill_hero remains the only roster removal path and must remain usable for expedition deaths; sacrifice guard precedes it. 3. 4. Safety/repeats: forecast emulates worst-case loss damage across Wave.from_zone using exact max HP, rounding, cumulative HP, and non-boss <=25% retreat rule including all traits/stats. Finite risky dispatch allowed with warning; infinite requires safe and rechecks before every repeat. total_runs is 1..999 including initial; 0 means infinite. Automatically bank every completed run and track cumulative stones/xp/items and runs_completed. Stop after casualty, retreat/failure, incomplete team, or stop_requested; stop means finish current. Captured membership/destination are immutable under preset edits.

5. Clock: persist per-order stable ID, deterministic run seed, initial duration and remaining_seconds. Use monotonic online delta; persist saved_at_unix for offline elapsed max(0, now-saved_at_unix). On load subtract offline time only from already-dispatched current runs; resolve each due run once, then start at most the next repeat at full duration in the open session. No recursive offline catch-up. Rollback gives zero offline progress; forward jump completes current run only. Stable due ordering is remaining time then order ID. Pulse about 0.25s; no per-frame save. Periodic timer/recovery save about 15s and durable dispatch/completion mutations. Pause-menu pause stops online delta; closing follows offline rule. UI observes backend scheduling and need not own it.

6. Exactly once: persisted seed drives deterministic local RNG through expedition/quick-resolve while preserving public resolve(team,wave) seam via helper/optional expedition entry. Defer existing signal-triggered saves during resolution and commit one atomic save containing casualties, cache, rewards, order advance, report. Atomic failure restores pre-transaction memory, preserves previous canonical save, sets notice, and cannot retry awards from mutated memory. Dispatch has the same durability. SaveService remains sole file owner; prevent from_dict/load autosave recursion and preserve newer-version refusal. Add actual isolated-APPDATA reload tests.

Any new cache pauses recovery_clock_paused. acknowledge_recovery_losses unpauses all current losses. Cache stores its created recovery-clock value. Legacy turn age maps to elapsed active minutes while preserving remaining effective window and migrated caches start paused. Parallel returns/dispatch do not age caches. design:
ASTRA IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — AUTONOMOUS SQUAD COMBAT AND RESCUE
2026-09-22. Product direction approved by owner: implement every suggestion in the squad-command design and downed/rescue follow-up; use Sol and Luna in parallel. This is the decision-complete implementation proposal. Implementation authorized and active: the owner explicitly removed the global mode blocker. This design is the accepted contract; runtime acceptance remains outstanding.

OBJECTIVE
Replace the future direct-control expedition direction with autonomous, watchable, commandable hero combat integrated with existing timed orders. Deliver standard five-hero expeditions, a 30-hero raid and a 50-hero regional mission, four archetype ability kits, configurable automation and supplies, downed revival, stranded-hero rescue/abandonment, and safe persistent watched/background/offline settlement. The existing action arena remains an isolated legacy practice scene until the new scene passes acceptance; the hub then presents RTS practice/watch as the primary combat surface.

DIRECTOR PRODUCT RULINGS
1. Heroes always handle basic attacks and role positioning. Auto Battle advances mission objectives; players may override orders at any time. Per-ability and per-item Auto/Manual preferences remain effective in either mode. Squad stances: advance, stay together, defend, protect ally. Direct orders take priority until fulfilled/cancelled. Tactical pause affects the watched battle only; leaving the view resumes it. No live speed multiplier in this implementation.
2. RTS controls: LMB selection/drag box, Shift additive selection, RMB contextual move/attack/guard/carry, Shift+A attack-move, H hold, G guard targeting, R retreat, Space battle pause, 1-9 squad selection and double-tap camera focus; WASD pan and wheel zoom. Selected hero/squad actions appear in one compact command panel. The battlefield uses orthographic perspective, authored ground/bounds, native chibi primitive meshes, class silhouettes, faction/selection rings, HP/downed markers, restrained skill effects and clear danger markers.
3. Existing archetypes receive one signature active and one passive, authored in Resources: Knight protection, Ranger piercing shot, Mage area burst, Rogue flank/interrupt. Automatic decisions use these exact kit rules. Ability data includes cooldown, range, effect/radius and magnitude; no new hero stat. The first consumables are healing and revival draughts; configured per-run allocations, auto-use conditions, last-revival reserve, and stockpile keep-at-least reserves. Consumables are escrowed at dispatch; unused allocations return once at settlement. Repeat refill must respect reserves and stop with a visible reason when it cannot satisfy the configured loadout.
4. Zero HP means downed, never immediate roster deletion in this backend. Living allies revive via the configured skill/item rules; any living ally in the full deployed force keeps the battle active. Victory secures all surviving/downed allies. Retreat extracts living heroes and downed heroes actually carried to the exit; unrecovered heroes become stranded. Downed heroes do not attack, move or consume supplies.
5. A full wipe or abandoned battlefield survivors creates a stranded incident. Hero IDs remain in the roster but are unavailable and protected, with equipment reserved. Player chooses rescue or explicit abandonment; no automatic rescue dispatch. A rescue team of up to five enters the preserved battlefield, reaches fallen heroes and extracts them. It can use revival or carry a downed hero to the exit. It need not kill every enemy. Extracted heroes are secured; withdrawn rescuers return; wiped rescuers join the stranded incident. Existing gear-cache recovery is a separate feature. Only final abandonment/expiry invokes the established Expedition -> GameSession.kill_hero removal/cache path.
6. Stranded incidents use active-play rescue time, separate from gear-cache state. New incident pauses its countdown for review; explicit Start rescue window starts it. Lifetime uses the existing authored 900 + 300*Reliquary seconds as a provisional starting value, not offline elapsed time. Failed attempts do not reset incident age. A deadline prevents dispatching new attempts once expired; an already-dispatched rescue is allowed to resolve. Original and later stranded heroes share the incident deadline. Closing the game never consumes this window. No passive rescue while unreviewed.
7. Reuse 1-5 member presets as squads. Standard zones permit one squad; the new Fallen Citadel raid permits up to six squads/30 heroes; Frontier March regional mission permits up to ten squads/50 heroes. Overlap is rejected before dispatch. The raid requires simultaneous control of three sites before its boss becomes vulnerable. The region contains camps, patrol groups, a defend/escort objective and extraction; it is an authored bounded region. AI assigns squads to objectives when Auto Battle is enabled. Large-party duration and enemy scaling use the zone's reference force size; existing zones retain reference size five, so increasing a new zone cap does not accelerate Verdant farming.
8. Current route/return timers remain a minimum reward-arrival gate. Battle victory can finish before return travel; rewards settle only after both objective completion and the route timer. Pausing/observing cannot credit rewards early. Watching and background play use one canonical simulation. Offline advancement affects only the already-dispatched leg; never chain repeat runs. Finite repeats stop on any downing, retreat, wipe, missing member, supply failure or request. Unlimited repeat requires a conservative unattended forecast using the same simulation and configured policies, rechecked before each repeat; never advertise the old statistical forecast as proof for the new engine.

TECHNICAL INTERFACES AND AUTHORITY
- New combat/battle/ domain files own typed RefCounted runtime state and static rules: BattleState, BattleActor, BattleOutcome, BattleSimulation. Definitions remain Resource data. BattleSimulation.create_run(team snapshots, zone, squads, policies, supply escrow, seed); advance(state, elapsed); issue_command(state, command); forecast(...); validate_snapshot(data); to/from_dict. Fixed logical tick 0.1s; stable actor ordering, explicit RNG state, bounded mission timeout and deterministic result. Advance must produce the same state for equal elapsed logical ticks regardless of render rate or view presence. Reuse Wave.from_zone for existing wave power instead of copying the ramp. Existing CombatResult stays unchanged for legacy arena/quick-resolve compatibility.
- BattleView consumes an order ID and read-only state snapshots, and emits commands through GameSession. It never awards loot, spends profile inventory, removes heroes or writes files. SceneRouter adds one BattleView destination plus an order-ID transition payload. No fourth autoload.
- GameSession remains profile coordinator: order dictionaries contain serialized battle checkpoints/escrow, not scene objects. Combat rules remain static in BattleSimulation. Explicit APIs: get_battle_snapshot(order_id), issue_battle_command(order_id,command), set_battle_paused(order_id,bool), dispatch_force(preset_ids,zone_id,total_runs,policies,loadout), dispatch_rescue(incident_id,preset_id,loadout), start_rescue_window(incident_id), abandon_stranded(incident_id). Existing dispatch_expedition wraps one squad for compatibility. Reservations include active and stranded heroes. Viewing/commanding validates current IDs and ownership every time.
- Save schema 3. New top-level supplies and stranded_incidents; orders add backend/battle/escrow/phase/squad membership. Every persistent actor is keyed by stable hero/enemy IDs; effects/cooldowns/orders/objectives/RNG/elapsed ticks serialize. No Hero/Node/Resource objects in JSON. v0/v1 retain the existing migration, then migrate to v3. v2 migration preserves identities, resources, presets, reports, outstanding run counts, seeds and minimum remaining travel. For an in-flight v2 order, create the new battle at its start and retain its remaining route timer; do not simulate imaginary prior combat, instantly grant rewards, or perform legacy immediate-death resolution. The revised ETA may include the newly simulated fight. Persist migration once atomically before play; malformed/future data blocks play/writes and preserves canonical bytes.
- Every command that consumes a resource or changes durable orders, completion, rescue extraction/abandonment and migration uses the established transaction boundary. Periodic battle checkpoints use existing cadence; no per-frame disk writes. Completion applies XP/loot/stones/zone clear/report/order advancement/resupply/refunds exactly once. Seeded loot uses existing Expedition.roll_loot and current reward helpers inside the transaction. Final hero removal stays exclusively routed through Expedition and GameSession.kill_hero. A save failure rolls back all profile/battle/resource changes and exposes its cause; reload retries the same outcome.
- Offline simulation is bounded by each mission's authored maximum logical duration, not wall-clock absence. It cannot run millions of ticks for a month away. An offline wipe creates a paused rescue incident. A tactical pause is view-session state and clears on closing/reopening the view; offline progress follows the saved automation settings. New commands override future decisions only; no reroll of already committed events.
- New timing, skill, supply and mission constants are provisional director-authored entries in SYSTEMS plus the existing balance/definition Resources before code consumes them. Workers do not invent balance, art direction, controls or failure policy. No new dependencies, network service, hero stat, autoload, paid wait, stamina, procedural world, multiplayer or custom AI scripting language.

BOUNDED PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATION
A. Sol owns combat/battle domain + hero ability definitions + pure simulation tests. Luna simultaneously owns BattleView scene/controller, procedural chibi visuals, selection/camera/UI against the frozen API. Neither edits profile/save/hub. Baseline copies and hashes precede edits; preserve ig-6l4 source. Engine use is exclusive and scheduled by Astra.
B. After domain API freeze, Sol owns profile/expedition/save/SceneRouter integration and migration, supply/rescue transactions and backend tests. Luna owns hub controls/preset force assembly, automation/loadout/rescue panels, watch/practice affordances and UI tests. Coordinate SceneRouter and unique-name contracts explicitly; no overlapping writes.
C. Fresh Sol independently reviews persistent state, death/rescue authority, replay/rollback and migrations. Luna may run bounded UI/performance harnesses while the review is read-only; Godot processes must never overlap. Astra reviews actual screenshots, logs and material findings. Repair findings within owner scopes, then run final affected acceptance on frozen production state.

ALLOWED FILES BY BOUNDARY
Domain: new combat/battle/battle_actor.gd, battle_state.gd, battle_outcome.gd, battle_simulation.gd; new combat/abilities/ability_definition.gd and four authored .tres; heroes/hero_definition.gd and existing four hero definition resources; zones/zone_definition.gd and two new zone resources; balance_table.gd/balance.tres when assigned; tests/unit/test_battle_simulation.gd and test_battle_rescue.gd.
Presentation: new combat/battle/battle_view.gd, battle_view.tscn, battle_unit_view.gd; project.godot for explicit input entries; tests/unit/test_battle_controls.gd. Native primitive meshes only initially.
Integration: systems/game_session.gd, save_service.gd, scene_router.gd; hub/expedition/expedition.gd and expedition_orders.gd; equipment/lost_cache.gd only if needed to preserve the existing distinct cache contract; hub/hub.gd, hub_ui_builder.gd, hub.tscn; relevant unit tests and tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd. Do not manually edit UIDs, tools or .godot. Astra alone owns docs/GAME_SPEC.md, SYSTEMS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, DECISIONS.md and KNOWN_ISSUES.md design amendments.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Five autonomous heroes finish a real authored encounter; player selection, squad commands, attack-move/hold/guard/retreat, pause, camera, manual skill/item and Auto toggles work through actual runtime input. Full-auto and an identical no-command watched run produce identical simulation outcomes.
2. Downed/skill revival/item revival/carry/extraction/full wipe/rescue success/partial rescue/rescue wipe/abandonment/active deadline are tested. Any living allied squad keeps a raid active. No downed hero is deleted. All final death paths preserve the single removal writer.
3. A 30-vs-30 runtime scene is measured for simulation and render performance; a 50-hero regional mission can deploy, navigate objectives and settle. Record actual hardware/frame metrics, actor counts and limits rather than claiming scalability from unit tests. No persistent crowd pile-up at objective/attack positions; commands remain responsive.
4. Timers/repeats/offline single-leg/reservations/favorites/bulk protections remain valid. New supplies respect allocation/reserves, save rollback and exactly-once refunds/consumption. Inspect a real repeat/refill and an unattended wipe.
5. Isolated actual disk v1/v2 migration and v3 reload at mid-fight, paused view, downed state, stranded incident, active rescue, partial extraction and completed order; RNG/cooldown/position/escrow continuity. Invalid IDs, duplicate reservations, malformed time/counters and future versions refuse load/write. Failed write preserves canonical bytes and retry outcome.
6. Final powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/import_gate.ps1 is clean, zero warnings/script errors. Full tools/godot/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_win64_console.exe --headless -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gdir=res://tests/unit -gexit passes. Run tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd and the isolated runtime/capture harnesses. Logs under .agent-results/logs; final screenshots under .agent-results/ig-544. All tests use isolated APPDATA. Confirm no Godot processes or LSP6005 listener remains.
7. End only when all accepted features are integrated and verified, not after an isolated prototype. Record any gameplay-feel tuning separately without presenting provisional balance as playtested. Close ig-544 and ig-yzc only when their replacement watch/command direction is actually delivered.
ASTRA CONTRACT ADDENDUM — resolves both read-only worker reviews
These exact rulings supersede ambiguous wording above and are accepted for the active implementation.

CLOCKS / MIGRATION / PAUSE
Route minimum and battle advance in parallel from dispatch. Active order phases are fighting, rescuing, or returning; a terminal battle enters returning until remaining_seconds reaches zero, then one settlement removes/repeats the order. A wiped battle can settle its stranded incident as soon as its terminal state is committed; it does not wait for an artificial trip home. UI calls remaining_seconds the route minimum while fighting, not a promised exact arrival. A repeat starts both a fresh full route and a fresh battle; excess delta is never spent on the next run. Standard encounter maximum is 180 logical seconds, raid 300, region 420; timeout ends as withdrawal, returns living actors, and strands downed actors not extracted. Offline route advances by all nonnegative elapsed time; combat advances by at most its remaining authored simulation bound, current run only. Recovery/rescue clocks never receive offline time.
For v2 migration: validate v2 using its original rules, transform stable fields, reduce its remaining route by max(now-old_saved_at,0) once, create new battle at logical tick zero, then atomically persist v3 with the new timestamp. No historical combat ticks are invented, even if the route is already zero. Do not then apply ordinary v3 offline advancement again. v0/v1 follow existing identity migration before this transform. Migration failure blocks play/writes and leaves canonical bytes intact.
Tactical pause is a nonserialized GameSession set of watched order IDs. It pauses combat ticks only, not the route minimum or other orders. Leaving the battle view, changing watched order, loading a profile, or restarting clears it. The paused-view reload test must assert resumed simulation with preserved durable combat state; it must not expect the pause flag to persist.

STATE AND UI CONTRACT
Canonical coordinates are Vector2(x,z) on a flat y=0 ground; standard bounds +/-20, raid +/-35, region +/-50. UI renders at Vector3(x,0,z); JSON positions/facing/order points are exactly two finite numbers.
BattleState fields: simulation_version=1, order_id:String, zone_id:String, kind:String(normal/rescue/practice), status:String(active/victory/retreated/stranded/timeout), tick:int, tick_remainder:float in [0,0.1), rng_state:String (decimal signed int64, never JSON float), elapsed_seconds:float, max_seconds:float, actors:Array[BattleActor], squads:Array[Dictionary], objective_state:Dictionary, supplies_remaining:Dictionary, policies:Dictionary, completed_waves:int, downed_ever_ids:Array[String], extracted_ids:Array[String], command_sequence:int. Godot RandomNumberGenerator is used; serialize its state as a validated decimal string to preserve all bits.
BattleActor fields: id:String, hero_id:String(empty for enemy), archetype:String, faction:String(ally/enemy), spawn_index:int, squad_id:String, position:Vector2, facing:Vector2, hp:float, max_hp:float, atk:float, defense:float, speed:float, crit_rate:float, crit_damage:float, life:String(alive/downed/extracted/dead; dead only for enemies), attack_range:float, move_speed:float, attack_cooldown:float, ability_cooldown:float, item_cooldown:float, order_kind:String, order_target_id:String, order_point:Vector2, carried_by_id:String, carrying_id:String, guard_target_id:String, ability_auto:bool, effect_state:Dictionary. Actor IDs and spawn_index are unique, stable and preserved through rescue snapshots. Effects include shield/guard duration, interrupt/stun duration and attack windup/telegraph fields needed by the view; UI does not infer authoritative damage from animation.
GameSession.get_battle_snapshot(order_id)->Dictionary returns a detached serialized snapshot plus transient paused:bool, route_remaining_seconds:float, team_name:String and last_command_error:String; empty if order absent. battle_changed(order_id:String) is emitted once per existing 0.25s process pulse or accepted command/settlement, not per actor. UI interpolates positions between snapshots; the scene never mutates the returned dictionaries to affect play.
GameSession.issue_battle_command(order_id:String, command:Dictionary)->Dictionary returns {accepted:bool,error:String,sequence:int}. Payload fields: kind:String, actor_ids:Array[String], target_id:String optional, point:Array[float] optional, value:String/bool optional. Kinds: move, attack, attack_move, hold, guard, carry, retreat, ability, item_healing, item_revival, set_stance, set_auto_battle, set_ability_auto, set_item_auto. Value kind is validated for each command. All actors must be current living allied actors owned by that order; target/ground/cooldown/range/supply preconditions are validated. Invalid commands reject atomically with a readable reason and no effect. One new direct movement/target order replaces that actor's previous direct order; idle completion returns it to squad policy. There is no custom command queue in this version.
Commands are applied atomically on receipt, stamped with current tick plus a monotonically increasing sequence. Movement affects the next tick; valid manual skills/items resolve once immediately and start cooldown only when their effect/resource consumption succeeds. Same-tick commands follow accepted sequence order. Automatic tick phases are: expire effects/decrement cooldowns; choose intentions; movement/local separation; support actions; offensive skills/basic attacks; extraction/objective/terminal evaluation. Each phase iterates stable spawn_index; support priority is revive skill, permitted revival item, healing, then offensive ability/basic attack. Damage immediately marks zero-HP allies downed and detaches carriers. Downed allies cannot be executed by enemies. Already invalidated targets consume no skill/item or cooldown.
Squads are {id:String,name:String,hero_ids:Array[String],stance:String,guard_target_id:String}.
